title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
why_read: An interesting robotics self-improvement framework that boosts task success rates substantially using simulation practice rather than retraining weights.
analysis: RPG is a framework where a robot system improves itself by practicing manipulation tasks in simulation, diagnosing failures using execution feedback and privileged simulator state, and refining a library of reusable skills and prompts without updating the underlying model's weights. The reported jump from 28.6% to 95% success over 15 practice rounds, and perfect physical trial results after calibration, is a notable result if it replicates. It's a good example of combining classical robotics practice loops with LLM-based skill coordination rather than pure end-to-end learning. The approach is somewhat complex and the real-world validation set is small (30 trials), so some caution is warranted on generalization.
